records.text: Washington County Sheriff Nate Brooksby abruptly resigned during an election, leaving one candidate, and his name was removed from the sheriff's website and social accounts without a public explanation.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It is. So this is interesting. Sheriff Nate Brooksby has resigned suddenly. He had like a COVID resignation, died suddenly, resigned suddenly. ... He resigned and now there's an interim sheriff in place and there's like I said they're in the middle of an election so now they're down to a single candidate. ... The resignation occurred on Friday and there has not been a public statement given for this out of nowhere resignation but over the weekend his name was quietly removed from the sheriff's office website and social media pages and there was a lot of speculation and I saw that some people said that there was going to be more information that was coming out.

verification.notes: The Washington County Sheriff's Office confirms Brooksby resigned on Friday, March 27, during the scheduled sheriff election, with an acting sheriff installed. The official notice was published March 30. The claims that his name was quietly scrubbed, that only one candidate remained, and that no explanation existed are not all established by the official source.

records.text: At 8:02 p.m. on September 11, a retired detective told Nate Brooksby that he knew who Charlie Kirk's shooter was and was trying to get him to surrender voluntarily.
records.speaker: Nate Brooksby

appearances.snippet: At exactly 8.02 on the 11th, I received a call from a friend of mine who happens to be a retired detective that worked for me for many years. ... So he said, hey, I know who Charlie Kirk's shooter is. I know the family through religious association. ... And he's in Washington County now, and we're working on trying to get him to come in voluntarily.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting of Sheriff Brooksby's press conference records that he said he received the call at exactly 8:02 p.m. from a retired detective who claimed to know the shooter and was working on voluntary surrender. Confidence is medium because this verifies Brooksby's first-person account, not an independently timestamped call record.
